info.name: CasaClean API
info.description:
QA test collection for the CasaClean backend API.

HOW TO USE:
1. Make sure the server is running (see api-testing/00-setup.md).
2. This collection has variables. Check the {} icon (top right) to see/edit them:
   - baseUrl: http://localhost:3000/api/v1  (change if your server runs elsewhere)
   - email / password: the user you sign in with
   - cityId / serviceId / specialRequestId / bookingId: filled in for you after you create each thing
3. Run requests in order: Auth > Signup, verify email by hand, Signin, then City/Service, Special Request, Booking.
4. The login cookie (lt) is kept automatically by Postman after Signin, so the
   admin requests just work as long as your signed-in user is an admin.

Note: requests that create a city, service, special request or booking automatically
save the new id into the matching variable, so the Get/Edit/Delete requests reuse them.
Booking notes: creating a booking needs a logged-in user (admin role not required), but
listing all / get-by-id / edit / delete are admin only. Create a special request first if
you want to test the specialRequests add-ons on a booking.

request.description: Create a new account. Expect 201. The account is NOT active until you click the verify link in the email (check your Mailtrap inbox).
Log in. Expect 200 and an 'lt' cookie. The user's email must be verified first, otherwise expect 403.

Confirm an email. Normally opened in a browser from the email link. Replace PASTE_TOKEN_HERE with the real token. This REDIRECTS (no JSON) to the client signin page with ?verified=success or ?verified=failed.
Send the verification email again. Always returns 200 with a generic message (on purpose, so nobody can find which emails exist).
Start Google login. Test this by hand in a browser (it redirects to Google's sign-in page).
Get your own profile. Needs the login cookie. Expect 200 with your user. Without a cookie expect 401.
Log out. Needs the login cookie. Expect 200 and the 'lt' cookie gets cleared.
Public. List cities with paging. Expect 200 with data.cities (a list), cityCount and length.
Admin only. Create a city. Expect 201. Name capital letter is fixed automatically. The new id is saved to the cityId variable for the other city requests.
Public. Get one city. Uses the cityId variable (set by Add City). Expect 200. Unknown id = 404, broken id = 400.
Admin only. Change only the fields you send. Expect 200. enabled:false should be honoured (off switch).
Admin only. Delete a city. Expect 200. Deleting again = 404.
Public. List services with paging. Expect 200 with data.services and serviceCount. Each service shows its full cities.
Admin only. Create a service offered EVERYWHERE. Expect 201, allCities true, cities empty. The new id is saved to serviceId.
Admin only. Create a service offered in ONE city. Needs a real cityId (create a city first). Expect 201. A fake city id = 400.
Public. Get one service. Uses the serviceId variable. Expect 200. Unknown id = 404, broken id = 400.
Admin only. Change only the fields you send. Expect 200. If you don't send coverage fields, the cities stay the same.
Admin only. Delete a service. Expect 200. Deleting again = 404.
Public. List the booking add-ons with paging, newest first. Expect 200 with data.specialRequests (a list) and specialRequestCount.

Admin only. Create an add-on. Expect 201. Name capital letter is fixed automatically. Enabled is true by default. The new id is saved to specialRequestId for the other requests (and the Booking requests).
Public. Get one add-on. Uses the specialRequestId variable (set by Add Special Request). Expect 200. Unknown id = 404, broken id = 400.
Admin only. Change only the fields you send. Expect 200. enabled:false should be honoured (a disabled add-on can't be picked on a new booking).

Admin only. Delete an add-on. Expect 200. Deleting again = 404. Note: if you want to test bookings with special requests, run the Booking requests BEFORE deleting (or re-create and re-enable the add-on).

Any logged-in user. Create a booking. Contact name/email come from your account (not the body). serviceId/cityId are NUMBERS. Status defaults to 'confirmed'. Expect 201. The new id is saved to bookingId.

To test add-ons, add a valid enabled id to specialRequests, e.g.: "specialRequests": ["{{specialRequestId}}"] (create one in the Special Request group first).
Any logged-in user. List ONLY your own bookings, newest first. Expect 200 with data.bookings (a list) and bookingCount. Without a cookie = 401.
Admin only. List ALL bookings (everyone's), newest first. Expect 200 with data.bookings and bookingCount. A normal user = 403, no cookie = 401.
Admin only. Get one booking. Uses the bookingId variable (set by Create Booking). Expect 200. Unknown id = 404, broken id = 400, normal user = 403.

Admin only. Change only allowed fields (status, dates, durationMinutes, cleaners, address, notes, supplies, specialRequests). status must be one of pending/confirmed/cancelled/completed. Fields like user/customerEmail are ignored. Expect 200.
Admin only. Delete a booking. Expect 200. Deleting again = 404. Normal user = 403, no cookie = 401.
Logged-in user. List only your own recurring subscriptions. Complete a recurring first booking through the payment flow before running this request. The first returned id is saved as subscriptionId.

item.name: Get Saved Cards (for subscription card update)

request.description: Logged-in user. Helper request for the subscription card-update test. The first saved card id is stored as paymentMethodId.
Owner only. Pause an active subscription. Requires the CSRF header and an empty JSON body. Expect 200 with pausedReason user-request.

exec: pm.test('subscription is paused for user request', () => {

request.description: Owner only. Resume a paused subscription after the server verifies that its stored card still belongs to the customer. Expect 200 and active status; a bad card returns 400.
Owner only. Point the subscription at another card owned by the same Stripe customer. Run Get Saved Cards first or set paymentMethodId manually. Unknown fields are rejected.
Owner only. Run this as a separate final scenario: it cancels future cycles but must not alter already-created paid Bookings.
Admin only. List all subscriptions. Add status=active, paused, or cancelled to filter. The first result can populate subscriptionId for the detail and admin-action requests.
Admin only. Returns the subscription plus its direct cycle Bookings and capped chargeAttempts history.
Admin only. Pause an active subscription. Run this before Admin Resume; use a separate active subscription from any cancellation scenario.
Admin only. Resume a paused subscription after its stored card passes the ownership check.
Admin only. Final-state scenario: cancel future cycles without changing existing paid Bookings.

item.name: Contact
item.description: The website contact form and the admin inbox behind it. POST /contact is the only unauthenticated write in the API, so it is guarded three ways: the X-Requested-With CSRF header, a 5-per-hour rate limit, and a hidden honeypot field. Sign in as an admin (Auth > Signin) before the admin requests.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Jane Cooper",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "phone": "+39 06 1234567",
  "topic": "general",
  "message": "Hello, I would like to ask about weekly cleaning for my flat."
}

request.description: Public - no login needed. The website contact form. Stores the message, then emails the team (CONTACT_NOTIFY_EMAIL) fire-and-forget. Expect 201; the new id is saved as contactMessageId. Rate limited to 5 per hour per IP.

exec: pm.test('a message id comes back', () => pm.expect(m).to.have.property('_id'));

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Spam Bot",
  "email": "bot@example.com",
  "topic": "general",
  "message": "Buy cheap things at my totally legitimate website.",
  "website": "http://spam.example"
}

request.description: Anti-spam. The hidden 'website' field is empty on the real form; a bot fills it. Expect the SAME 201 as a real submission - but nothing is stored and no email is sent. Confirm with 'List Contact Messages' afterwards: Spam Bot must NOT be there.

exec: pm.test('the body looks exactly like a real acceptance', () => {

request.description: Bad email, unknown topic and a message under 10 characters. Expect 400 with per-field errors.
Admin only. The inbox, newest first. Optional ?status=new|handled (enable the query param). Expect 200 with contactMessages plus contactMessageCount.
Admin only. One message by id. Expect 200, or 404 for an id that does not exist.

exec: pm.test('it is the message we sent', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.contactMessage.email).to.eql('jane@example.com'));

request.description: Admin only. status is the ONLY writable field - the text belongs to the customer, so sending 'message' or any other key is a 400. Expect 200 with handledAt and handledBy set; send status 'new' to reopen and clear both.

exec: pm.test('marked handled, stamped with who and when', () => {

request.description: Admin only. Emails the answer to the customer, records it on the message and marks it handled - one step. 'body' is the ONLY field you send; recipient, subject and the quoted original come from the stored message. The send is AWAITED, unlike the arrival notification: if the mail host is down you get 502 and nothing is recorded.

exec: pm.test('the reply is on the thread', () => pm.expect(m.replies).to.have.lengthOf.at.least(1));
pm.test('replying also marks it handled', () => pm.expect(m.status).to.eql('handled'));

request.description: Admin only. Expect 200 the first time and 404 if you run it again.
